title: Big-O hid a real 40x slowdown from me and I want to complain about it
author: midnight_compiler

replies.author: segfaulter
replies.body:
This is also why the "linked list vs array" question has a boring answer in practice. Textbook says O(1) insertion for the list. Reality says you paid a cache miss to find the insertion point and another to follow the next pointer, and the array won by memmoving 200 bytes that were already in L1.

Bjarne has a talk where he benchmarks exactly this and the vector wins up to absurd sizes.

replies.author: heap_of_trouble
replies.body:
Fair, but I'd push back slightly on the framing. Big-O isn't hiding anything, it's answering a different question: how does this scale as n grows without bound. Your 40x is a constant. Make N ten times bigger and both versions get 100x slower.

It's a real limitation but it's the documented one. The mistake is treating it as a performance model rather than a scaling model.

replies.author: midnight_compiler
replies.body:
> The mistake is treating it as a performance model rather than a scaling model.

Ok that's a better way to put it than anything in my post. Stealing that.
